s: The Dasavatara Temple at Deogarh belongs to which period?

The Dasavatara Temple at Deogarh (Uttar Pradesh) is one of the finest surviving temples of the Gupta period (6th century CE). Dedicated to Lord Vishnu, it is considered an early and classic example of Nagara-style temple architecture. The temple is famous for its exquisite sculptures depicting the ten incarnations (Dashavatara) of Vishnu and represents the high artistic achievements of the Gupta Age, often called the Golden Age of Ancient India. Hence, the correct answer is Option (1).

• Architecture → Early Nagara Style

x: In the Panchayatan style of temple making, there were four subsidiary shrines along with the temple of the principal deity. The main temple was square with an elongated mandap in front of it, giving it a rectangular shape. The subsidiary shrines were placed opposite to each other on either side of the mandap, giving the ground plan a cruciform shape.
